decision.summary: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and maintained its ongoing asset purchase programs.

changes.quote: Household spending has advanced a bit more quickly, but growth in business fixed investment has slowed.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted slight acceleration in household spending while business investment growth cooled.

changes.quote: Inflation recently picked up somewhat, reflecting higher energy prices.
changes.explanation: Policymakers acknowledged a recent uptick in inflation driven by energy costs.

changes.quote: The Committee remains concerned that, without sufficient policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.
changes.explanation: The Fed slightly tweaked its language to maintain its ongoing concern regarding sluggish labor market improvements.

changes.quote: To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee will continue purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month.
changes.explanation: The Committee transitioned its phrasing from agreeing to start a new program to continuing its ongoing monthly purchases.

changes.quote: Voting against the action was Jeffrey M. Lacker, who opposed additional asset purchases and disagreed with the description of the time period over which a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate and exceptionally low levels for the federal funds rate are likely to be warranted.
changes.explanation: One official dissented against both the ongoing asset purchases and the forward guidance timeline.

tone_quotes.quote: Growth in employment has been slow, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.
The Committee remains concerned that, without sufficient policy accommodation, economic growth might not be strong enough to generate sustained improvement in labor market conditions.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 12.06% APR costs about $50.25 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.8% and moved +1 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.39% would rise by about $1.66 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.8%, and employers added an average of 168k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.9% over the past year (September 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.7%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved 0 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.04% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will maintain its highly accommodative monetary stance until the labor market improves substantially. Educational forecast model data indicates a 74 percent probability of a hold at the next meeting.

citations.detail: In particular, the Committee also decided today to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent
